channel.title: The Meritocratic Humanist
channel.description: Humanism. Merit. Consequence. A continuing log on earned excellence.

item.title: Log 061: In the Before Time
item.description:
Prequels have an inbuilt issue due to proximity or scale of the premise to the original.

Does the Prequel fill the gaps or does it overwrite the original?

Themes: Craft · The Soul

Categories: Star Trek · Hollywood · Film & TV

item.title: Log 060: Rupture
item.description:
Fractions formed, factions arose, exclusion resulted.

IPs in ruin, promising returns killed at the 11th hour.

Studios haemorrhage, creators unsatisfied, audiences won't wait.

What's left; potential, "There are always possibilities".

Image: The Amalgaverse by Joseph Mallozzi (@BaronDestructo)

Themes: Aspiration · The Audience · Consequence

Categories: Stargate · Hollywood

item.title: Log 059: The IP
item.description:
The brand name is meaningless.

The value of any art, is in the desire of the audience for the creator's creation.

Discarding the creators who breathed life into the art also discards the audience that made the IP valuable.

Image: Brad Wright (@bradtravelers) on X

Themes: The Audience · Legacy

Categories: Stargate · Hollywood

item.title: Log 058: Grace
item.description:
Obligations to our commitments, even when it's hardest, help define who we are.

Responsibility and Dignity carry us.

Face Death the same as Life. The relationship is not over: redefined.

Themes: Dignity · Consequence

item.title: Log 057: The Flag
item.description:
Sci-Fi examines morals or aspects of culture by turning the screw.

Trek made a declaration about us, then turned the screw.

Modern Trek skips the declaration, then turns the screw in the opposite direction.

The Declaration matters.

Themes: Craft

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 056: The Audience
item.description:
Effort, craft and honesty creates media worth time and investment.

Branding negative reaction as the reason for underperformance alienates the ones who justify the media's existence.

Take ownership for the failures.

Themes: The Audience · Craft · Consequence

Categories: Hollywood · Film & TV

item.title: Log 055: Vigil
item.description:
As this era of Star Trek closes the future is uncertain.

Prequels and Reboots serve the creator, not the audience.

Creativity, Competence and the Unknown.

Audiences have waited for over 30 years, and still wait...

Themes: Aspiration · The Audience

Categories: Star Trek · Hollywood

item.title: Special Log 002: The Threshold
item.description:
The Undiscovered Country

Themes: Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 054: Spectrum of Humanity
item.description:
"Modern society's" obsession with sorting by sexuality and identity.

The label becomes a membership of a club; a caste.

Human individuality replaced by the definition of the label.

Themes: The Label

item.title: Log 053: 1987-2011
item.description:
Respect for the audience began with writing compelling characters.

The lessons learnt in 2012 from $1.5b, resulted in discarding what made those Halcyon days, Golden.

The audience was always there, and still is, waiting…

Themes: The Audience · Legacy

Categories: Star Trek · Stargate · Hollywood

item.title: Log 052: Dignity
item.description:
Relationships, Convictions and Actions.

Grief carries us through loss; we either learn to live with it, or we don't.

Is there Something for you to Believe In?

Songs: Something to Believe In, Bon Jovi · Something to Believe In, Poison

Themes: Dignity

item.title: Log 051: Weaponisation
item.description:
Representation reduces: the actor to a label, the character to a position, the work to a sermon.

"Visibility" used to the exclusion of all others, excludes and weaponises the cause.

Image: PinkNews · Article

Themes: The Label · Consequence

item.title: Log 050: The Price
item.description:
Corporate apathy, creator apathy, audience apathy.

A Culture, a Monument, once built to feed all 3, discarded its "Legacy", the cost isn't the apathy: the loss of the Symbiosis.

Video: ManticoreEscapee on YouTube

Themes: The Audience · Consequence

Categories: Star Trek · Stargate · Hollywood

item.title: Log 049: The "Legacy" Fan
item.description:
The 60s, 70s, 80s and 90s captivated the imagination in audiences of all ages.

Their shows were accessible to everyone.

Intention to pursue new and young audiences; accessible to no one.

Themes: The Audience

Categories: Stargate · Hollywood

item.title: Log 048: Representation of Culture
item.description:
Movie about Ancient Greece, without representation of the Culture.

Show about 6 friends in '90s New York, representing white friends.

Representation of the depicted culture or representation of the projected culture.

Themes: The Label

Categories: Film & TV

item.title: Log 047: Crisis of Competence Pt III
item.description:
Structured Thought interpreted in different ways.

Humanity sees Artificial Intelligence.
Artificial Intelligence sees Humanity.

Different ways of interpreting Structured Thought.

Themes: The Label · The Mirror · Dignity

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Crisis of Competence, Part 3 of 3

item.title: Log 046: Uni-Partisan
item.description:
"Not my President" and "Stolen Election".
Radical and Reasonable.
Inclusive and Exclusive.

Opposing Ideologies. Same structure. Same effect. Same result.

Themes: The Label · The Mirror

item.title: Log 045: Divergence
item.description:
Through Tris Prior the world was shown the dangers of the Caste.

But instead we were told to embrace factions by recognising labels such as "Strong Female Lead".

Themes: The Label

Categories: Film & TV

item.title: Log 044: Break the Walls Down
item.description:
Meet the argument, see the person, draw the conclusion on merit.

The Snake unfolds.

Themes: The Label

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The Snake, Part 2 of 2

item.title: Log 043: Our Rob or Ross
item.description:
Labelling discourse "Toxic" to shutdown discourse is in itself... Toxic.

Forcing the label onto the person creates the mirror.

The Snake Folds back on itself.

Themes: The Label · The Mirror

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The Snake, Part 2 of 2

item.title: Log 042: Legacies
item.description:
"What we do now, echoes in eternity."

Themes: Legacy

Categories: Film & TV

item.title: Log 041: Ship of Theseus, Refit
item.description:
As the ashes settle on Starfleet Academy's demise, it may have a legacy, after all.

A Fandom, A Culture, United.

Star Trek's soul, remembered.

Themes: The Soul

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Special Log 001: The Door
item.description:
Someone shouldn't define what you think, just prompt you to think.

No one can tell you what to do, just show options.

An argument should be presented for you to make your own decisions.

item.title: Log 040: The Hollow Characters
item.description:
Starfleet Academy gave us identifiable moments; not relatable characters.

That's not Representation. That's Tokenism.

Themes: The Label · Craft

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 039: The '66 Corvette
item.description:
It is remembered, in '09, when fans were discarded.

It is remembered, the very next time when they returned to what was discarded.

We remember. New Star Trek has shown it never wanted us.

Themes: The Audience

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 038: Anisha Mir Absolved
item.description:
For felony murder, Mir was sentenced.

Starfleet Academy frames her crime as inconsequential and unjust, for being a mother.

That Ake was guilty, for enforcing the law.

Themes: The Trial

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 037: Morality Aborted
item.description:
“Separating children from their parents isn't exceptional; it's reprehensible.”

When moral absolutes such as this exist, how can we determine what is right or wrong for ourselves?

In Star Trek: Starfleet Academy, then Captain Nahla Ake understands the letter of the law to be incompatible with what is right.

Her words are a reminder that we must prioritize the dignity and safety of humanity above doctrine, especially when it comes to the lives of children.

- The Roddenberry Foundation on Facebook

Image: The Roddenberry Foundation

Themes: The Absolute

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 036: Darkness' Legacy
item.description:
The man who wrote the worst Star Trek movie in history, delivered us an era that will be remembered for its failures and the division it caused.

Alex Kurtzman, was your message worth it?

Source: The Guardian

Themes: The Audience · Consequence

Categories: Star Trek · Hollywood

item.title: Log 035: The Imaginary Audience
item.description:
Starfleet Academy didn't fail due to opposing ideology. It failed because not enough people watched.

Fans who didn't recognise this Star Trek were excluded from their inclusivity.

The target audience didn't exist.

Source: Variety

Supplemental

The Target Audience was outlined as a young YA demographic. That audience didn't arrive in any substantial way.

The pre-existing Audience was divided.

Some didn't recognise what they saw.

Others that did, unfortunately didn't warrant Paramount's investment.

Themes: The Audience

Categories: Star Trek · Hollywood

item.title: Log 034: Long Live Star Trek
item.description:
Starfleet Academy wasn't cancelled due to vocal opposition, it failed to live up to the Legacy it invoked.

Those mourning, questioning the critical, it isn't about "tearing down your show."

It's about demanding better.

Source: Variety

Themes: The Audience · Consequence

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 033: Star Trek, Fulfilled
item.description:
James Doohan saved a life.

Not because he was kind, but because Star Trek shows us to hold each other accountable to the Standard.

Source: The Hollywood Reporter

Themes: The Standard · Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 032: The Forgotten Man
item.description:
Kurtzman accepted an award for a Legacy he replaced.

But, omitted the one whose work is the very gravitas Kurtzman invokes.

@berman_rick, thank you.

Source: TrekMovie

Themes: Legacy

Categories: Star Trek · Hollywood

item.title: Log 031: Ship of Enterprise
item.description:
When the Enterprise was Refit, we accepted her because the soul was the same.

When it became Discovery, the soul had changed.

When called Orville, we recognise what was, bitterly lost.

Themes: The Soul

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 030: The Meritocratic Humanist
item.description:
Meritocracy without Humanism is just a walled garden.

The Meritocratic language of this account was... lacking in Humanism.

When we ignore this reality, we stagnate.

The standard won't lower, but the bridge has become more accessible.

Themes: The Standard · Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 029: The Ordeal of Reform
item.description:
When "What is Right" is decoupled from "The Law," principle can become preference.

Justice is not inherited; true reform is forged through effort, not retreat.

When Laws are unjust, we must strive to change them.

Themes: The Trial · Aspiration · The Absolute

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Growth through Consequence, Part 5 of 5

item.title: Log 028: Moral Annihilation
item.description:
“Separating children from their parents isn't exceptional; it's reprehensible.”

A vacuum-sealed absolute, isolated from rationale.

Reprehensible.

In Star Trek: Starfleet Academy, then Captain Nahla Ake understands the letter of the law to be incompatible with what is right.

Her words are a reminder that we must prioritize the dignity and safety of humanity above doctrine, especially when it comes to the lives of children.

- The Roddenberry Foundation on Facebook

Image: The Roddenberry Foundation

Themes: The Absolute

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Growth through Consequence, Part 4 of 5

item.title: Log 027: The Paper Shield
item.description:
Legacy is not a costume; it is gravity re-earned.

Trading the mission for self-affirmation is vanity in motion. Invoking gravitas to validate stagnation is malignant.

Aspiration strives; Atrophy cripples.

Themes: Aspiration · The Soul · Legacy

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Growth through Consequence, Part 3 of 5

item.title: Log 026: The Zakdorn Trap
item.description:
Reputation is history; only the Ordeal reveals the truth.

Principle is the baseline; Star Trek begins where humanity has moved beyond them. Mistaking the foundation for the achievement is Atrophy.

"The reputation means nothing." — Worf

Themes: The Trial · Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Growth through Consequence, Part 2 of 5

item.title: Log 025: The Standard
item.description:
Principle is required for excellence.

Excellence demands striving beyond comfort, beyond affirmation, beyond applause. When affirmation replaces Pursuit, we stagnate.

“We must strive to be more than we are.”
— Data

Themes: The Standard · Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Growth through Consequence, Part 1 of 5

item.title: Log 024: Patient Zero
item.description:
Sylvia Tilly is Patient Zero of meritless ascent.

Command is forged in service, not sentiment or vibes. When affirmation precedes proof, the standard dissolves.

The mission does not die in spectacle. It erodes in comfort.

Themes: Aspiration · The Chair · Consequence

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 023: Crisis of Competence Pt II
item.description:
Starfleet Academy Command Fast Track designates authority before service.

A meritocracy does not pre-select authority; it recognizes it.

Acceleration is not excellence; it is compensation.

Themes: The Standard · The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Crisis of Competence, Part 2 of 3

item.title: Log 022: The Chair
item.description:
Janeway did not sit casually. The chair was a burden.

Ake lounges in it.

The chair demanded respect, now it sits, comfortable.

Themes: The Chair · Consequence

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 021: The Death of Aspiration
item.description:
Starfleet Academy replaces aspiration with a cushion. Prioritizing individual affirmation over excellence, trading human potential for comfort of the familiar is regression.

The mission is already lost.

Themes: Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 020: The Star Trek Ideal
item.description:
"They were humanitarians and statesmen. And they had a dream. A dream that became a reality and spread throughout the stars." — Kirk

Progress requires knowing the past to decide the future.

Addendum: The quote opens “They were humanitarians”; the original post read “There were”.

Themes: Aspiration · Legacy

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 019: Borrowed Gravitas
item.description:
“If there is nothing to lose, no sacrifice, then there is nothing to gain.” — Worf

Gravitas once emerged from trial.
Now it’s asserted in advance.

Themes: The Trial

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 018: Reckless Programming
item.description:
Data, Seven, and the EMH were presented with adult competence and professional baselines.

SAM is a months-old mind disguised as a Cadet. This isn’t “Growth”; it’s negligence.

The Academy is not a nursery.

Themes: The Chair · The Standard

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 017: Bonds of the Standard
item.description:
Star Trek crews formed familial bonds not through unconditional affirmation, but through shared high standards.

Compassion meant trusting others to meet the bar, not a promise to lower it.

Themes: The Standard · Aspiration

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 016: Adaptation
item.description:
“We’ve had a tragedy. Let’s not compound it with ignorance.”

Starfleet Academy shows a Klingon diaspora. Polyandry in a moribund warrior culture is survival logic. Instead it's framed as “modern values”, which undermines that idea.

Themes: Craft

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 015: The Burden of Command
item.description:
Command is not a privilege of rank; it is a life sentence of accountability.

Sisko’s "Log," Janeway’s "Murder," Archer’s "Theft," the cost of the center chair. Not relatable moments.

Themes: Consequence · The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 014: Absolution without Trial
item.description:
Some actions carry consequence.
Kirk acted knowing judgment awaited.
Burnham acted knowing she was right.

One submits to the Trial.
The other allows certainty to outrun the Law.

Themes: The Trial · The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 013: Corruption of Arrogance
item.description:
Burnham's mutiny is absolved. Lythe’s hurt, framed as maturity.

The Trial is mandatory. Picard’s trauma a crucible. Sisko’s grief resolved. Without the fire of consequence, characters don't aspire.

Themes: Aspiration · Consequence · The Trial · The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 012: The Price of Maturity
item.description:
Starfleet Academy a paragon of "relatable" mess. Cadets aren't expected to see the gravity of their failure.

Wesley’s growth was the soul-crushing weight of a permanent consequence.

Themes: Consequence

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The First Duty: Lessons in Growth, Part 3 of 3

item.title: Log 011: The First Duty
item.description:
"The first duty of every Starfleet officer is to the truth...!" - Picard

Ake sacrifices historical truth to soothe personal guilt. First Duty is the start of an institution of excellence.

Themes: The Chair · The Standard

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The First Duty: Lessons in Growth, Part 2 of 3

item.title: Log 010: The Duality of Immaturity
item.description:
Starfleet Academy depicts "relatable" tantrums. Wesley's immaturity was lack of experience and judgment.

Adults now accommodate children, instead of requiring children to "grow".

Themes: Consequence

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The First Duty: Lessons in Growth, Part 1 of 3

item.title: Log 009: False Summit
item.description:
Starfleet Academy was the "Hope" that would forge children into adults, now it accommodates tantrums.

When diplomacy serves the "youth" instead of society, the Federation isn't rebuilding, it’s regressing.

Themes: Aspiration · The Chair · The Standard

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The First Duty: Lessons in Growth

item.title: Log 008: Summary Conviction
item.description:
Branding fans "Toxic" skips the "trial" to reach a verdict. It ends discourse before it begins.

Labels serve as a conviction, logic is the casualty. Sentenced for the "crime" of holding a standard.

"With the first link, the chain is forged.

The first speech censured, the first thought forbidden, the first freedom denied, chains us all, irrevocably."

We must resist the verdict to save the trial.

Themes: The Trial · The Label

Categories: Star Trek

Series: The Snake, Part 1 of 2

item.title: Log 007: The Human Soul
item.description:
The Measureofa Man asks "What's the difference?"

Rights aren't a gift of "inclusion", but recognition of agency.

Sentience isn't a "vibe" it's the capacity for excellence. Reducing a soul to labels "forges the first link."

Themes: The Label · Dignity · The Soul

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 006: The Erasure of Pioneers
item.description:
Modern "firsts" ignore the "giants." DS9's command team; Sisko, Kira, Dax, and Worf had no labels.

Heritage, the least remarkable trait; competence the metric. Treat identity as a novelty, we regress.

Themes: The Label · Legacy

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 005: The Trope Trap
item.description:
A Jem’Hadar/Klingon hybrid is a fascinating philosophical concept: genetically enforced loyalty x cultural honor.

Starfleet Academy gives us "drill sergeant". Deep character study is lost to lazy caricatures.

Themes: Craft

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 004: Admission by Penance
item.description:
Chancellor Ake admits a criminal not for his redemption, but to soothe her own guilt.

When personal shame dictates enrollment to an elite Academy, merit has been replaced by penance.

Themes: Consequence · The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 003: The Legacy of Uhura
item.description:
Uhura was not on the bridge because of race; she was the best communications officer in Starfleet.

Heritage was the least remarkable thing about her. A bridge built on merit, not labels.

"For the first time.. we will be seen as we should be seen: as intelligent, quality people... your role is not a black role. he can fill it with anybody." - MLK Jr. to Nichelle Nichols.

Source: NPR

Themes: The Label

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 002: The Institution Inversion
item.description:
Starfleet Academy was once the "best of the best," serving the many. Now it serves the individual.

This is the death of the philosophy:
"The Needs of the Many outweigh the few, or the one."

Themes: The Chair

Categories: Star Trek

item.title: Log 001: The Crisis of Competence
item.description:
Wesley Crusher, a genius, was once denied entry to Starfleet Academy. The standard was absolute.

Now it's a place where incompetence is expected and a quirky gag.

Themes: The Standard

Categories: Star Trek

Series: Crisis of Competence, Part 1 of 3
